fields.h1: Build a Giveaway Landing Page From Entry to Winner
fields.hero_description: Build a giveaway landing page that counts entries, adds bonus entries for referrals, and saves each one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Runs Behind Each Giveaway Page
fields.features_subheading: Visitors see a prize and one entry form. These six parts cover what happens after someone presses Enter.
fields.feature_1:
The page and its entries from one prompt

Describe the prize, who may enter, and the closing time. Emergent builds the giveaway page, its entry form, and the table behind it, then changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Bonus entries for referrals

Each entrant gets a personal link. When a friend enters through it, the referrer gets the number of bonus entries you set, and the page shows every person their current entry count.
fields.feature_3:
One entry per email address

The form checks each email against the entries table, so a second entry from the same address is not counted again. You decide if the form refuses it or shows the first entry.
fields.feature_4:
Entries that reach your CRM and Slack

Built apps connect to any tool with an API, so each entry can update a HubSpot contact. Set a rule, and entries that match send a Slack or email alert to the person who follows up.
fields.feature_5:
A live count of entries by source

The dashboard behind the page updates as each entry arrives. Split it by source link to see which post, email, or partner brought in the most entries before the giveaway closes.
fields.feature_6:
Run it on your domain, keep the code

Publish the giveaway on your own domain, which is included and uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository and stays ready for the next giveaway.

fields.tab_content_1:
Each friend who enters adds 3 bonus entries

Saltmarsh Coffee Roasters is giving away 12 bags of coffee, one a month for a year. Every entry counts once, and each friend who enters through an entrant's link adds 3 bonus entries to that entrant. After 4 friends entered through Wren Halvorsen's link, she holds 13 entries. Each entry saves to the entries table.
fields.tab_content_2:
One of 2,847 entries drawn at Sunday's close

Brindlecrest Outfitters closes its tent sweepstakes on Sunday at 11:59 PM ET. The prize is a 2-person tent, and the form takes one entry per email. When entries close, the app draws one of the 2,847 entries at random and sends the winner email. Ottoline Marsh won, and her row in the entries table is marked Winner.
fields.tab_content_3:
The cake with 412 votes at Friday's close wins

Cinderbloom Bakery let its customers pick the winner of its cake decorating contest. Each entrant uploads a photo of the cake, and visitors vote once per email. At Friday's close, Hollis Penrose leads with 412 votes, ahead of Bram Ellery at 388 and Sunniva Clark at 301. Her cake wins a class with the head baker.
fields.tab_content_4:
Booth entries from shops of 25 or more go to a rep

Tenpenny Field, software for HVAC contractors, gives away a drone at booth 214. Visitors scan a QR code to enter. Each entry lands in HubSpot tagged Booth 214, and shops of 25 or more technicians send sales rep Anouk Vey an email. Coldwater Mechanical entered with 31 technicians.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Giveaway Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Use these seven steps to create a giveaway landing page that counts every entry and picks a winner when entries close.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the prize and its value
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the rule that picks the winner
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set the close time and time zone
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put the prize in the headline in plain words, such as 12 bags of coffee or a 2-person tent, and add its retail value if you know it. Visitors decide in a few seconds whether to enter, and the prize does the work a slogan cannot.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose what counts as an entry: an email on a form, a photo upload, or a vote. Ask only for what you need to reach the winner and follow up afterward. Each extra field is one more reason for a visitor to close the tab.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide whether the winner is drawn at random or chosen by judges or votes, and state that rule on the page. If friends can earn bonus entries, give the number per friend. Entrants should be able to check their own count against it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the closing day, hour, and time zone on the page, such as Friday at 5 PM PT. Use the same time in your official rules and in every post that links to the giveaway. Entries that arrive after it do not count toward the draw.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the giveaway in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the prize, the entry rules, and the close time into one prompt. Emergent builds the page, the entry form, and the entries table behind them. Prompt again to change any part, such as the thank-you screen an entrant sees after entering.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Enter five times with test addresses, including the same email twice and one entry through a referral link. Check that the repeat is not counted again and that the referrer's count goes up. Delete the test rows before the page goes live.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and hand out source links
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page on your domain at least a week before the close. Give each partner and influencer a link of their own, and the dashboard shows which source brought in each entry. When the giveaway ends, name the winner on the page itself.

faq_plan.q: What is a giveaway landing page?
faq_plan.a: A giveaway landing page is a single page built to collect entries for a prize. It names the prize, explains how to enter and when entries close, and holds the entry form. Every link you share for the giveaway points to it, and each entry lands in one list.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a giveaway landing page?
faq_plan.a: Create one by settling the prize, the entry method, and the close time first, then building the page around them. Describe all three to Emergent's AI landing page builder, and it builds the page with an entries table behind it. Test it with a few entries before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in giveaway landing page examples?
faq_plan.a: Look at what happens after someone enters, not only at the design. The strongest giveaway landing page examples name the prize first, show the close time with a time zone, and tell each entrant how to earn more entries. Check whether the page confirms the entry on screen, since that is the moment an entrant decides to share it.

faq_plan.q: What do the best contest landing page examples have in common?
faq_plan.a: They name the prize, the judging rule, and the deadline above the fold, and they ask for little more than the entry itself. Photo and video contests add a gallery of entries, which shows new visitors what they are up against.

faq_plan.q: How is a sweepstakes landing page different from a skill competition?
faq_plan.a: A sweepstakes awards its prize by chance, while a skill competition is decided by judging or voting. One definition calls a sweepstakes a procedure for awarding a prize that is based on chance. On a sweepstakes landing page, put the close time and the draw method next to the form. On a skill competition page, publish the judging criteria before the first entry arrives.

faq_plan.q: What do competition landing page examples show about judging entries?
faq_plan.a: They put the judging rule on the page before the first entry. Name who judges and the criteria, or say that public votes decide and each email gets one vote. A contest landing page that shows each entry's vote count gives entrants a reason to share their link. On a page built with Emergent, every vote is a row in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Is a giveaway landing page template better than describing the page in a prompt?
faq_plan.a: A template is faster only when your giveaway matches its layout and fields. A prompt starts from your own prize, entry rule, and close time, and Emergent builds the page and the entries table to fit them. The next giveaway is one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do referral bonus entries work on a giveaway landing page?
faq_plan.a: The page tracks who referred whom: an entry that arrives through an entrant's personal link adds a set number of bonus entries to the referrer. If you also award entries for social posts, ask entrants to tag them. The FTC says that making the word "contest" or "sweepstakes" part of the hashtag should be enough. Put the hashtag in your entry instructions.

faq_plan.q: How does a giveaway landing page pick and notify the winner?
faq_plan.a: It draws one entry at random from the entries table when entries close, marks that row, and emails the winner. A contest uses the judges' scores or the vote count instead. Draw a backup winner at the same time, and give the first winner a reply deadline before you move to the next name.

faq_plan.q: What is a good entry window for a contest landing page?
faq_plan.a: Start with 2 weeks, and extend to 4 only if entries are still climbing in the second week. If the prize is tickets, close the contest before sales end and send everyone else to the event landing page. Name the winner within a week of the close, both on the page and by email.

plan.angle: The top 10 is screenshot galleries (Dribbble, Behance, Pinterest), example listicles from giveaway plugins and store builders, and template catalogs (KickoffLabs, Leadpages, ConvertFlow). They show what the page looks like and stop at the entry form. This page shows four giveaways running end to end: bonus entries for referrals, a sweepstakes that closes and draws one winner at random, a photo contest decided by public votes, and a trade show giveaway that sends big accounts to a sales rep. The FAQ covers examples, templates, sweepstakes versus contests, bonus entries, the draw and the entry window. Event and PPC landing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
